guide.title: Moment tensors and contraction planning
guide.summary: exact dense, sparse and factored moment and joint count tensors per group (no forced Cartesian expansion; exact conversions, marginals, slices, permutations, outer products), and bounded tensor networks contracted along the cheapest admissible order chosen through the FND-008 planner from exact per-step shapes, bytes and lifetimes, over-budget intermediates refused.

TENSOR-001.cpu: Native C (math_tensor.c): exact retained multi-index states over an FND-004 scope, per group: moment tensors T_g[i] = sum w prod_k x[col_k[i_k]] of order 0..8 over per-axis column lists (the constant 1 allowed; listwise, or SQL with per-entry contributing-row counts; axes sharing one column list accumulate their sorted multi-indices only) and joint count tensors over categorical axes (scope or explicit domains, NULL a slot of its own, weighted or not), with the selected and contributing rows kept apart from NULL validity; dense, sparse (CSR, strictly increasing multi-indices) and factored (declared rank-one sums with int64 factors, built without expansion) forms with exact conversions preserving order, dimensions, axes, groups, rows, counts and entries; marginalization, slicing, permutation, outer products, ungrouping and entry access in any form; int128 entries proven before any row is read (N x max|w| x prod_k max|x| <= 2^127 - 1) and every derived sum checked; a chunked builder (init, accumulate, merge, finish) that gives the same state bit for bit for any chunking; budgets (variables, degree, tensor, states, support, bytes) checked before allocation.
TENSOR-001.gpu: CUDA kernels math_tensor_gpu.cu (tr_mgpu_tensor_build): dense moment work items (entry, row slice) accumulate locally and add with the exact two-word atomic (symmetric tensors on their canonical entries, then a copy launch); count work items add one atomic per row; sparse builds insert every emission into an open-addressing table of at least twice the capacity (a local 64-bit compare-and-swap claims a slot) whose occupied slots the host sorts into the canonical CSR; the readback is adopted by tr_tensor_from_states after shape, row, order and bound checks; equal to the CPU bit for bit.
limitations: Entries are limited to 128 bits (refused beyond); orders up to 8, at most 64 columns per axis, dimensions below 2^32 and fewer than 2^64 cells per group.
A factored form's bound is a conservative sum over its terms, so some factored operations refuse what the dense form computes; count tensors have no factored form.
The CPU loops are single-threaded; the device sparse build sorts its hash table on the host.

TENSOR-002.cpu: Native C (math_tensor.c): networks of 1..8 TENSOR-001 tensors with named indices (at most 16 labels; a grouped tensor's group label first) contracted by Einstein summation along orders of pairwise steps: every order enumerated when there are at most max_orders (default 64), otherwise a bounded search (the greedy orders, then depth-first ones); each order with the CPU dense, CPU sparse (operands matched on their shared labels, products sorted and reduced) and CUDA dense kernels; exact per-step labels, dimensions, cells, summed combinations, stored entries (sparse: exact upper bounds), bytes, scratch, live bytes by materialization lifetime, the peak, the output bytes and a magnitude bound per step proven before execution; exact amounts per FND-008 cost component costed and budget-checked by tr_planner_choose (the family's own rates passed as the planner's override table), the cheapest admissible candidate chosen and rejected candidates kept as evidence with their refusals; execution of any admissible candidate returns the exact tensor with the actual per-step entries, bytes and peak.
TENSOR-002.gpu: CUDA kernel math_tensor_gpu.cu (tr_mgpu_tensor_contract): the dense candidate's pairwise steps, one work item per result entry evaluating the shared tr_tensor_dense_entry (exact int128 products and sums; every step bound re-proven on the host before copying), intermediates kept on the device and freed after their consumer; equal to the CPU kernels bit for bit.
limitations: No factored contraction kernel: factored operands are expanded (costed and budgeted); the CUDA contraction is dense only (sparse candidates run on the CPU).

Sparse sizes in a plan are exact upper bounds, not the data's actual supports; the rates are hand-set estimates in relative work units (not calibrated times); traces within one tensor are not supported.
